Top medical equipment suppliers in Canada include national distributors and large-scale providers like [Medline Canada](https://www.medline.ca/), which serves acute care and home health, [The Stevens Company](https://www.stevens.ca/) for clinics and hospitals, and online superstores like [CanMedDirect.ca](https://www.canmeddirect.ca/) for direct home delivery. [](https://www.medline.ca/)

- **Medline Canada:** Offers acute care, long-term care, and home health medical equipment with nationwide distribution and regional offices.

- **The Stevens Company:** A Canadian family-owned distributor providing surgical tools, hospital furniture, and clinic supplies.

- **[Global Medical Products](https://globalmedical.ca/):** Specializes in advanced institutional medical equipment and replacement parts for hospitals and long-term care.

- **CanMedDirect.ca

Focuses on direct-to-consumer and home-care medical supplies shipped across all provinces and territories.

- **[Ontario Medical Supply (OMS)](https://oms.ca/):** Supplies mobility equipment, home healthcare products, and clinical essentials.

- **[Vereburn Medical](https://vereburn.com/):** Distributes first aid, diagnostic tools, and mobility aids online. [](https://www.medline.ca/)

Canadian Hospital Specialties (CHS Ltd.)
is a Canadian manufacturer and distributor of critical care and hospital medical products, but
they do not manufacture consumer or digital remote wearables like continuous glucose monitors, smartwatches, or sleep trackers
. Those digital health tools belong to the broader consumer and remote patient monitoring (RPM) market.

Wearable Health and Remote Monitoring Types
Continuous Glucose Monitors (CGMs):
Devices like Dexcom or Abbott FreeStyle Libre that track interstitial glucose trends.
Smartwatches & Wearable ECG:
Consumer or medical-grade wrist devices that log heart rates, single-lead ECGs, and irregular rhythms.
Sleep Trackers:
Rings, bands, and watches measuring sleep cycles and rest quality.
Remote Patient Monitoring (RPM):
Home setups using cellular or Bluetooth devices (blood pressure cuffs, scales, glucometers) to stream data to clinical teams.
